newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka allows brokers to trade on own account.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka allows brokers to trade on own account.

text.p: The Colombo Stock Exchange said in a statment on Wednesday that it was permitting brokers to trade on their own accounts in a bid to boost market liquidity and raise broker incomes.
"We have passed the rules and now expect brokers to apply to be eligible," Dylan Moldrich, director general of the exchange told Reuters.
Brokers applying for the facility will require a minimum net capital of 10 million rupees, the statement said.
Net capital is made up of shareholder funds minus market value or cost of the portfolio, whichever is lower, and debts owed to the firm, it said.

Brokers trading on their own accounts will be able to buy only up to two percent of the issued capital of a single security and are barred from buying its own shares or those of its parent, associate or subsidiary.
"I believe we should have three to four brokers trading on their own accounts by May," Moldrich said.
